name: Connections Academy
line: Connections Academy, an online school, teaches math as a course. In AMP, assessment, teaching and review are continuous.
description: AMP vs Connections Academy: an online school that teaches math as a course, and a math program where assessment, teaching and review are continuous.
verdict: Connections Academy is a full-time online public school. Math is one course in it, taught through daily lessons, live classes and teacher-graded work, with benchmark assessments and state tests [3][5][7]. In AMP, assessment, teaching and review are continuous: every answer updates the learner's level and sets the next problem, and each problem carries its own hint, lesson and worked answer.

reasons.title: Continuous assessment
reasons.body: AMP has no separate test and no test day. It places a learner from their first answers, and every answer after updates the learner's level in that part of math and sets the next problem. Connections Academy places students in courses using their academic records. Its teachers evaluate student work, and students take benchmark assessments during the year and state tests [3].

reasons.title: The problem is the unit
reasons.body: In AMP, everything hangs off the problem in front of the learner: a hint that gives the first step, a lesson with a worked example, a video lesson, the worked answer afterward, and links to the skills it builds on and leads to. At Connections Academy the unit is the course: daily lessons and assignments set out in a planner [5], lessons in text, video and audio, and live LiveLesson classes where teachers reinforce challenging concepts [7]. Across 55 studies, worked examples improve performance in math [14].

reasons.title: Feedback on every answer
reasons.body: After every answer AMP shows whether it was right, the correct answer and the worked steps. At Connections Academy, teachers evaluate student work, and the Learning Coach gives one-on-one help and checks understanding [3][4]. Across 40 studies of computer-based feedback, in a mix of ages and subjects, feedback that explains had the largest average effect [13].

reasons.title: A level for each part of math
reasons.body: AMP keeps a separate level for each part of math, from counting through precalculus on one map of skills. A learner further along in geometry than in fractions gets work at both levels, and repeated misses send practice back to what a skill builds on. Connections Academy teaches by course and grade. It places students in courses from their academic records, and advanced younger students may work at a higher grade level when appropriate [3][6].

reasons.title: Continuous review
reasons.body: In AMP, learned skills come back in ordinary practice, at growing intervals, mixed with other math. A Connections Academy student follows the course's daily lessons and assignments [5], with benchmark assessments during the year and state tests [3]. We found no scheduled return to earlier math in the pages we read [3][5][9]. In a randomized trial with 787 seventh graders, mixed and spaced practice scored 62% a month later, against 38% for practice in blocks [12].

reasons.title: What the adult does
reasons.body: In AMP the adult does not plan, teach or grade. Parents and teachers see a level for each part of math and the actual problems behind every number, and each lesson has a guide for the adult. Connections Academy asks a Learning Coach, a parent or trusted adult, to oversee schoolwork about 5 to 6 hours a day in elementary school and 2 to 3 hours in middle and high school. The coach structures the day, gives one-on-one help and checks understanding [4].

theirs: Connections Academy is a full-time online public school program from Connections Education, part of Pearson. Its schools run state by state, for kindergarten through grade 12 [1]. Math is one subject in a full curriculum that the school says meets state standards. Course choices vary by school [3].

Students learn about 30 hours a week. Elementary students spend about 30% of the school day on a computer and 70% offline; middle school is about 75% online and high school 90% [5]. The day mixes live LiveLesson classes, where teachers reinforce challenging concepts, with independent lessons and assignments shown in a planner [5][7]. A parent or other trusted adult serves as Learning Coach, and certified teachers teach and evaluate the work [3][4].
credit: Certified teachers, and live online classes where they reinforce challenging concepts [3][7].
A Learning Coach at home gives one-on-one help and checks understanding [4].

theirs: We found no study of how much Connections Academy students learn, in math or any subject, on its curriculum or accreditation pages, in Evidence for ESSA or in What Works Clearinghouse intervention reports [6][8][10][11].
ours: Two findings bear on this comparison. In a randomized trial with 787 seventh graders that meets What Works Clearinghouse standards without reservations, mixed, spaced practice scored 62% on the researchers' own test a month later, against 38% for practice in blocks [12]. A meta-analysis of 40 studies of computer-based feedback, across ages and subjects, found the largest effects for feedback that explains [13]. AMP applies both at every problem.

AMP's own outcome studies are planned: growth on a national test against hours of use, then comparison groups, then randomized trials. Each will be registered before it starts and published whatever it finds. The research behind each part of AMP is in our report, and AMP is open source.

them: You want a full-time school with live classes and teachers who evaluate the work.
amp: You want assessment, teaching and review in the same practice, with no separate tests.
You want a hint, a lesson and the worked answer at every problem.
You want learned skills to keep coming back in practice.
Your child is at different levels in different parts of math.
You want math the adult does not have to plan, teach or grade.

questions.question: How is AMP different from Connections Academy?
questions.answer: Connections Academy is a full-time online public school. A learner follows a course's daily lessons and live classes, and teachers evaluate the work, with benchmark assessments and state tests [3][5]. AMP has no separate test: every answer sets the next problem, each problem carries its own teaching, and learned skills return in ordinary practice.

questions.question: Does Connections Academy work?
questions.answer: We found no study of how much its students learn, on its curriculum or accreditation pages, in Evidence for ESSA or in What Works Clearinghouse intervention reports [6][8][10][11].

questions.question: Can a learner use both?
questions.answer: Yes. They are separate programs. AMP places a learner from their first answers, whatever school they attend.
